spans.s:
Sṛṇī¤ is found certainly in one, and probably also in two other passages of the Rigveda. The sense appears to be ‘sickle.’ In one other passage sṛṇya is coupled with jetā: the sense is doubtful, Roth conjecturing cetā, and Oldenberg pointing out that chettā is also possible. Hopkins thinks that a ‘hook’ is here meant.
Foot notes i. 58, 4, where sṛṇyā, according to Geldner, Vedische Studien, 1, 116, n. 1, and to Pischel, ibid., 2, 111, stands for sṛṇyābhiḥ, and, as an adjective agreeing with juhūbhiḥ, means ‘sickle-shaped sacrificial ladles.’ But this is very doubtful.
